items.title: The Single Answer
items.question: Philosophers agree the Ship of Theseus has exactly one objectively correct answer discoverable by sharper thinking.
items.correctExplanation: False. No experiment settles it: answers track criteria (material, continuity, function), and criteria are chosen, not found. Genuine indeterminacy, not confusion.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Sharper thinking clarifies options without crowning winners: plank-ship, restored-ship, neither — each follows some legitimate criterion. Underdetermination is the finding.
items.lessonContent:
Criteria chosen, never found, decide puzzles.
Underdetermination is itself a finding.
Sharper thinking clarifies without crowning.
Genuine indeterminacy differs from confusion.
Share this: leave one ship undecided.

items.title: The Rival Hull
items.question: If Theseus's discarded planks get reassembled into a second ship, a genuine rival claimant to ship-identity exists.
items.correctExplanation: True. Hobbes's addition: continuity-of-matter and continuity-of-form diverge, crowning different winners. Rivalry is structural, not verbal.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Reassembly splits criteria that coincided: spatiotemporal continuity favors the repaired ship, material continuity the rebuilt one. Two winners, one name.
items.lessonContent:
Coinciding criteria can diverge later.
Reassembly manufactures rival claimants.
Structural rivalries outrun verbal disputes.
Two winners may share one name.
Share this: build one rival hull.

items.title: The Parfit Reversal
items.question: Parfit argued that personal identity is not what fundamentally matters — psychological continuity and connectedness matter more.
items.correctExplanation: True. Identity matters derivatively; what we care about in survival is continuity of mind. Reasons and Persons reorients the whole debate.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Parfit's reversal: stop asking 'is it me?' and ask what relations hold. Identity's importance was the assumption, not the conclusion.
items.lessonContent:
Assumptions hide inside questions asked.
Continuity matters more than identity.
Reorient debates, never just answer.
Relations outrank labels in survival.
Share this: prize one continuity today.

items.title: The Split Path
items.question: If your psychology branched into two continuers tomorrow, identity (a one-to-one relation) could not follow both — yet both would continue you.
items.correctExplanation: True. Branching breaks one-to-one identity while preserving everything identity was supposed to secure. Logic constrains labels, not lives.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Both branches psychologically continue you, but 'is identical to' cannot split: something other than identity does the mattering work. Fission exposes the gap.
items.lessonContent:
Labels constrain; lives continue regardless.
One-to-one fails where branching succeeds.
Continuers outnumber identities always.
Gaps exposed teach more than theses.
Share this: imagine one branch kindly.

items.title: The Body Verdict
items.question: Sameness of body alone settles every personal-identity puzzle: same organism always means same person.
items.correctExplanation: False. Teletransportation, fission, and prince-cobbler cases divide bodies from persons: organisms persist where persons arguably don't. Bodies underdetermine selves.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Amnesiacs, replicas, and exchanged minds all press the gap: same flesh, disputed self. Organisms anchor much but settle little.
items.lessonContent:
Flesh anchors much, settles little.
Persons divide where bodies persist.
Underdetermination haunts bodily criteria.
Organisms and selves part ways.
Share this: separate one body from self.

items.title: The Copied Self
items.question: Suppose surgeons copy every memory of yours into a fresh brain while you survive the operation. The copy is uncontroversially you.
items.correctExplanation: False. Copying creates branching puzzles, not settled identity: two claimants, one past. Duplication divides what memory was supposed to unite.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Perfect copies generate controversy, never consensus: original plus replica equals a fission problem. Memory copied is identity questioned.
items.lessonContent:
Copies generate controversy, never consensus.
Duplication divides memory's unities.
Branching puzzles outlive copying tech.
Two claimants share one past here.
Share this: meet one replica calmly.

items.title: The Prince Remains
items.question: In Locke's thought experiment, a prince waking with all his memories in a cobbler's body is still the prince — memory carries the person across bodies.
items.correctExplanation: True. Locke's verdict: consciousness, not flesh, makes the prince — bodies are costumes persons change. Memory bears identity across matter.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Prince-memories in cobbler-flesh stay princely by Locke's lights: sameness of consciousness defines sameness of self. Costumes change; wearers persist.
items.lessonContent:
Costumes change; wearers persist here.
Consciousness defines selves, not flesh.
Memory bears persons across bodies.
Thought experiments test criteria sharply.
Share this: wear one costume lightly.

items.title: The Officer's Loop
items.question: Reid's brave officer remembers the flogged boy, and the general remembers the officer — but the general forgot the boy. Memory transitivity breaks down.
items.correctExplanation: True. A remembers B, B remembers C, yet A forgets C: remembered-by fails transitivity, so it cannot be identity. Loops break chains.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Reid's circle — boy, officer, general — proves memory continuity isn't transitive like identity must be. Chains snap where loops close.
items.lessonContent:
Transitivity tests all identity claims.
Circles snap chains thoughtlessly assumed.
Remembered-by fails logic's bar here.
Loops break what lines require.
Share this: forget one link gracefully.

items.title: The Divided Hemispheres
items.question: If each hemisphere were transplanted into a new body, both recipients would psychologically continue the original — a genuine fission problem.
items.correctExplanation: True. Wiggins's fission: two continuers, one original — identity cannot follow both. Thought experiments need no scalpels.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Hemispheres separated carry psychology doubled: both recipients remember being you. One-to-one identity cannot cover two continuers.
items.lessonContent:
Thought experiments need no scalpels.
Doubled psychology defeats single identity.
Continuers outnumber originals here.
Fission problems are logic, not surgery.
Share this: split one self hypothetically.

items.title: The Closest Heir
items.question: Nozick proposed identity follows the closest continuer — the candidate most continuous with the original, provided no equally close rival exists.
items.correctExplanation: True. Closest-continuer theory adds the no-rival clause: win by continuity, lose ties to branching. Nearness decides, ties destroy.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Nozick's formula handles fission by disqualifying ties: closest alone inherits. Continuity ranks candidates; rivalry voids victories.
items.lessonContent:
Continuity ranks; rivalry voids victories.
Closest alone inherits the name.
Ties destroy what nearness builds.
Formulas handle fission elegantly.
Share this: rank one continuer closely.

items.title: The Perfect Chronicle
items.question: Narrative theories of identity require life stories to be perfectly accurate histories without omission or embellishment.
items.correctExplanation: False. Schechtman's articulation constraint demands intelligibility, not perfection: selves narrate selectively. Accuracy constrains loosely.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Narrative identity needs coherent self-telling, never flawless chronicle: selection and shaping are the point. Stories organize; they need not photograph.
items.lessonContent:
Coherence constrains; perfection never required.
Selection shapes selves legitimately.
Stories organize, never photograph.
Intelligibility suffices for identity.
Share this: narrate one day coherently.

items.title: The Psychology Claim
items.question: Animalism — the view that we are fundamentally human animals — identifies each person with their psychology rather than their organism.
items.correctExplanation: False. Animalism says the reverse: you are the living organism, psychology or not. Inverting it states the opposition's view.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Olson's animalism anchors persons in biology: organisms persist through coma, dementia, and dreamless sleep. Psychology rides; animal endures.
items.lessonContent:
Biology anchors what psychology rides.
Organisms persist through mental gaps.
Inversions state opposition views.
Anchor persons in living animals.
Share this: thank one organism today.

items.title: The Amnesiac Test
items.question: Profound permanent amnesia most threatens memory-based theories of identity, while animalism absorbs it with ease.
items.correctExplanation: True. Memory criteria strain where organisms persist: the amnesiac living body challenges recollection theories precisely. Theories differ in fragility.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Amnesia divides criteria cleanly: recollection views lose their grip, animalism keeps holding the body. Test cases sort theories by what breaks them.
items.lessonContent:
Test cases sort theories by breakage.
Recollection strains where bodies persist.
Fragility differs across criteria hugely.
Amnesia divides memory from organism.
Share this: hold one body theory.

items.title: The Double Proof
items.question: Split-brain research conclusively proves that every such patient houses exactly two distinct persons.
items.correctExplanation: False. Split-brain shows divided access, not settled headcounts: one, two, or fragmented — interpretations divide. Proof overclaims what data suggests.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Hemispheres semi-independent does not equal persons doubled: unity, duality, and disunity all have defenders. Data suggests; it never settles headcounts.
items.lessonContent:
Data suggests; it never settles.
Access divided differs from persons doubled.
Interpretations divide where data ends.
Headcounts exceed evidence always.
Share this: count one self carefully.

items.title: The Unchanged Nation
items.question: Nations persist as the same entity only while keeping identical membership — new citizens create new nations.
items.correctExplanation: False. Nations survive total turnover routinely: institutions, territories, and stories persist while members change. Membership flows; nations abide.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Japan, Egypt, France outlived every founding member: continuity lives in institutions, not rosters. Identical membership never defines nations.
items.lessonContent:
Institutions outlive all rosters fully.
Continuity lives beyond membership.
Turnover never ends nations.
Rosters flow; entities abide.
Share this: outlive one roster.

items.title: The Newborn Firm
items.question: A company replacing all staff, products, and premises legally becomes an entirely new entity automatically.
items.correctExplanation: False. Legal continuity survives total turnover: charters, debts, and brands persist. Law tracks institutional threads, not personnel lists.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Ship-of-Theseus firms keep charters while changing everything concrete: debts follow entities, not employees. Identity here is paperwork that binds.
items.lessonContent:
Paperwork binds across total turnover.
Charters outlive staffs and products.
Debts follow entities, never employees.
Legal threads persist materially.
Share this: incorporate one continuity.

items.title: The Dissolved Vow
items.question: Marriages that change utterly in habits, homes, and feelings automatically dissolve as legal entities.
items.correctExplanation: False. Vows persist through total transformation until dissolved by act: law ignores inner weather. Entities outlast their contents.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Changed feelings never auto-dissolve bonds: marriage persists as commitment structure through metamorphosis. Contents change; containers hold.
items.lessonContent:
Containers hold through content change.
Vows persist past feelings' weather.
Structures outlast their fillings.
Dissolution needs acts, never moods.
Share this: hold one container steady.

items.title: The Soul Criterion
items.question: Locke made sameness of immaterial soul the criterion of personal identity across time.
items.correctExplanation: False. Locke explicitly sidestepped souls as unknowable: consciousness and memory, not substance, define persons. Souls untestable cannot criterion-make.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. The Essay refuses soul-talk for persons: same consciousness, same self — substance unknown and irrelevant. Memory, never metaphysics, decides.
items.lessonContent:
Untestables cannot criterion-make.
Consciousness defines; substance waits.
Souls sidestepped deliberately here.
Memory decides, metaphysics watches.
Share this: sidestep one unknowable.

items.title: The Settled Upload
items.question: If mind uploading ever worked, it would empirically settle all personal-identity debates at a stroke.
items.correctExplanation: False. Uploads inherit the debates: is the upload you, your heir, or a replica? Technology stages puzzles; theory still judges.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Working uploads would instantiate fission, branching, and continuity questions — not answer them. Engineering executes; philosophy evaluates.
items.lessonContent:
Engineering stages; philosophy judges still.
Working tech inherits old puzzles.
Replicas raise, never resolve, questions.
Uploads need theories to mean.

items.title: The Gradual Swap
items.question: Replacing neurons one by one with functionally identical silicon preserves all continuity-based intuitions about survival.
items.correctExplanation: True. Moravec's gradual replacement keeps psychology continuous at every step: no moment of death occurs. Sorites-style continuity persuades where sudden swaps alarm.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Stepwise substitution preserves function, memory, and behavior throughout: observers detect no break. Continuity intuitions survive gradualism intact.
items.lessonContent:
Gradualism preserves intuitions fully.
Stepwise swaps avoid death-moments.
Continuity persuades where leaps alarm.
Observers detect no breaks ever.
Share this: swap one neuron hypothetically.

items.title: The Accountable Self
items.question: Locke tied personhood itself to accountability — persons are forensic entities, fit for reward and punishment.
items.correctExplanation: True. 'Person' is a forensic term for Locke: consciousness extends responsibility across time. Accountability defines the category.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Rewards and punishments need owners persisting: personhood exists for justice's purposes. Forensic needs shape metaphysical categories.
items.lessonContent:
Justice needs persisting owners.
Forensic purposes shape categories.
Accountability defines personhood here.
Responsibility extends with consciousness.
Share this: own one past act.

items.title: The Flowing Same
items.question: Heraclitus's river persists as the same river precisely through constant change of waters — identity as process, not material.
items.correctExplanation: True. Same river, different waters: process identity accommodates flux that material identity forbids. Flow constitutes sameness here.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Stepping twice differs because waters differ — yet riverhood persists as patterned flow. Processes abide while materials pass.
items.lessonContent:
Patterns abide while materials pass.
Flow constitutes sameness here fully.
Processes persist; stuff streams.
Riverhood outlasts water drops.
Share this: step one river twice.

items.title: The Seven-Year Body
items.question: Popular wisdom says the body replaces all its cells every seven years, making you physically brand new on schedule.
items.correctExplanation: False. Neurons, heart cells, and oocytes persist for decades or life: turnover varies wildly by tissue. No universal renewal clock exists.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Gut linings turn over in days; cortical neurons endure for life. Seven-year renewal is myth arithmetic on mixed tissues.
items.lessonContent:
Tissues turn over on separate clocks.
Neurons endure; linings refresh weekly.
Myths average what varies wildly.
No universal renewal exists.
Share this: keep one lifelong neuron.

items.title: The Gradual Guarantee
items.question: Some claim gradual silicon replacement guarantees survival on every theory of identity, including animalism.
items.correctExplanation: False. Animalists may deny it: replacing organism parts with silicon eventually replaces the animal itself. Guarantees fail across theories; intuitions vary.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Gradualism persuades continuity theories while animalism counts remaining organism: guarantees need unanimity theories never grant. Persuasion differs from proof.
items.lessonContent:
Unanimity never grants guarantees.
Persuasion differs from proof always.
Theories divide gradual cases too.
Organisms count against silicon majorities.
Share this: doubt one guarantee.

items.title: The Told Self
items.question: Narrative theories hold that selves are constituted by the self-stories their subjects tellingly endorse and live by.
items.correctExplanation: True. Selves as self-told stories: endorsement plus enactment constitute identity narratively. Living the tale makes the teller.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Narrative views ground persons in owned stories, not substances or bare memories: telling shapes being. Endorsed tales constitute tellers.
items.lessonContent:
Tales constitute tellers who endorse.
Endorsement plus enactment makes selves.
Stories shape beings telling them.
Living tales makes tellers real.
Share this: tell one self truly.
